name: sg-benday
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's benday: a regular screen of flat pop-art dots over newsprint cream, each dot taking its tone from a colour field drifting underneath, so blocks of colour roll across the grid without the grid ever moving.

colors.description: Four dot tones the drifting colour field blends between. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette. The cream ground is a constant inside the shader and does not follow this.

dots.description: Dots across the frame; lower is a coarser, bolder screen. Upstream default, range 8 to 90.

flow.description: Drift rate of the colour field under the screen; 0 freezes the colour blocks. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.2.

size.description: Dot radius as a fraction of its cell, so how much ink the screen lays down. Upstream default, range 0.1 to 1.

deviations.what: The four u_palette dot tones are ours, not upstream's `prism` preset.
deviations.why: benday/meta.json names a palette as a string only; the table it resolves against lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Ours is a high-key pop set picked so near-black copy clears 4.5:1 over any dot, which a fully saturated primary set does not.

deviations.what: No post chain: upstream's poster runs grain 0.04, vignette 0.16, contrast 1.05 and saturation 1.12 over the shader output.
deviations.why: The post chain is also in @shader-gallery/runtime. Our output is the raw shader, so it will not match the upstream poster. The section's own CSS grain layer covers the banding the poster's grain was there for.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
